stories.notes: Empty acceptance criteria and null spec on a complex multi-platform (GO, UP, MX) live preview feature. openspec needed to elaborate ACs and define real-time preview architecture; speckit needed to harden testability, security (preview token exposure, unauthorized draft access), and edge cases (draft vs published state, multi-locale preview).

agentContributions.notes: Live Preview is a novel capability — the codebase currently fetches only published content via useContent (236 callers). No preview-mode logic, preview API route, or Contentstack live-preview SDK integration exists. The attachment point is the useContent hook, which is the single chokepoint for all content retrieval. Because acceptance criteria are empty and the description is minimal, VCs are derived from the description's intent: enabling CMS authors to see draft content before publishing.

Openspec provided zero acceptance criteria — only context notes explaining that Live Preview is a novel capability with no existing preview-mode logic. All 20 criteria above were derived from the story title, description, technical file list, and openspec's context notes. Key areas covered: (1) Core preview behavior — activation, draft retrieval, real-time updates (AC-1 through AC-3); (2) No-regression for the 236 existing useContent callers (AC-4, AC-5); (3) Error handling — invalid tokens, API failures, missing/deleted draft content (AC-6, AC-7, AC-17, AC-18); (4) Security — draft content isolation outside preview context (AC-8); (5) Session management — persistence across navigation, exit behavior (AC-9, AC-10, AC-19, AC-20); (6) Accessibility — screen reader announcement, color contrast, non-color-only indicator (AC-12, AC-13); (7) Multi-codeline coverage — gotransit, upexpress, metrolinx including file-name variants noted in technical notes (AC-14, AC-15, AC-16); (8) ContentstackLink behavior in preview context (AC-11). IMPORTANT CAVEAT: File contents were not available for inspection. The ACs assume that useContent is the sole content retrieval chokepoint (per openspec's note about 236 callers) and that ContentstackContext is the provider that would hold preview configuration. If the actual file contents reveal a different architecture (e.g., multiple content retrieval paths, or ContentstackContext not being the right attachment point), some ACs may need adjustment. The story description is extremely minimal ('[GO, UP, MX] Live Preview of Content in CMS') — additional requirements may exist that were not captured here.

coordinatorReview.reviewNotes: Two concerns: (1) OpenSpec produced zero acceptance criteria — its contribution was purely contextual (identifying useContent as the 236-caller chokepoint, noting no preview-mode logic exists). SpecKit then had to derive all 20 ACs from the minimal story title/description and openspec's context notes, effectively doing openspec's job. The collaborative pipeline did not function as designed; openspec failed to elaborate requirements. (2) SpecKit explicitly states 'File contents were not available for inspection,' meaning all 20 ACs were written without examining the actual codebase — the ACs assume useContent is the sole content retrieval path and ContentstackContext is the right attachment point, but these assumptions are unverified. The story JSON provided contains no technicalNotes.files field, so no repository path verification could be performed. A human reviewer should confirm the architectural assumptions (useContent as sole chokepoint, ContentstackContext as preview config holder) against the actual code before implementation begins.
